judged.rule: The hook completes both action slots with specific words the visuals can show: “Kalo kamu {first action}, {temporal connector} kamu {second action}, kamu sudah punya {system}. Tapi {problem}.” The first action starts on visibly bare or empty materials or at an unused site, the named first version is in use, and the problem describes what the keeper sees. Write the finished lines with ordinary punctuation.

After the premature first system the script runs at least two problem–improvement rounds: each improvement answers a problem shown just before it and is tested on screen, and each later problem differs in kind from the earlier ones.
Earlier changes stay legible in the same site and landmarks through to the finished system.

Before the income scene the system is shown stable: it copes with a condition that broke an earlier version, or one last action runs through the completed setup, and the result depends on improvements the viewer saw added.

After the system is shown stable and before the closing wide view, one scene shows the first output weighed or counted beside the finished system, with a small price tag hung in the scene reading quantity × dated local price ≈ gross value, labelled “estimasi”; no profit, payback or income promise is made.
The runtime is carried by visible construction changes, operating checks and consequences (seven to nine events as a starting map); every finished component is shown being brought into the build.

The narration ends with a congratulation naming the built result, then a next-build question containing the consecutive phrase “bikin di halaman”; the opening has no channel intro and nothing asks for a follow.

On the closing question the words “bikin di halaman” stay yellow to the end of the line and a small account handle fades in beneath the caption; the film then cuts to an end card that exactly matches the episode thumbnail, held 0.5 s delivered.
Scale or subject state changes when the viewer needs new information: a push-in or cut for a reveal, tracking along a route, a return to wide for the finished system.
In each view the decisive vessel or interaction fills at least 40% of the frame width and keeps a landmark when reframed.
